entry_state: An acquired derivative's paid starting value is separate from later hedge gain. Instrument reductions retain gains accumulated before removal and send only later changes on removed fractions outside the hedge; instrument identity changes the result even at an equal nominal ratio. The purchase and settlement bridge is complete. The next subsection begins partial cessation of the purchase itself.
exit_state: Partial purchase cessation retains a stopped reserve and sends subsequent owned-instrument changes to profit. Homogeneous proportional allocation is justified separately from the narrower origin-matched derivation. Expectation changes and unrecoverable losses release only the remaining signed reserve; gross settlement and liquidity checks close the conditional histories. General heterogeneous attribution remains open.
findings: The homogeneous allocation states the common origin and proportional valuation assumptions before using the lower-of scaling identity.
The stopped reserve survives loss of high probability while the purchase remains expected; cancellation and unrecoverable-loss findings have separate effects.
The different-origin example derives one traceable attribution under exact matching and no historical ineffectiveness, explicitly retaining the relationship-level calculation.
The cash/basis identity and funding example distinguish terminal balance from sufficient cash at each payment. No new confirmed local defect.
